summary.title: Building Your Own Personal Learning Curriculum
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a self-directed developer learning plan by deriving goals from job specs, splitting skills between work and home study, setting realistic measurable targets, and staying accountable to a mentor or buddy.
keywords: job specs to set learning goals
time tracking for study with toggl
how do i structure extracurricular learning
takeaways: Use job postings from target companies to find the skills that matter most, then look for commonalities.
Split the skill list into things you can learn at work and things you must study in your own time.
Set small, measurable, realistic weekly targets and increase them only after you have found a rhythm.
Find a mentor or a peer buddy to hold you accountable and provide validation.
Build small scratch pad projects to turn course material into working knowledge.
summary.summary: Kirsty Simmonds describes how she built a personal learning curriculum after a bootcamp and her first developer job, when she struggled to choose among many frameworks and courses. The article walks through steps: gather 'dream job' specs to identify priority skills, split those skills into at-work and at-home learning, and recommend resources such as CS50, Frontend Masters, FreeCodeCamp and Udemy. It then covers setting realistic targets with time tracking (she used Toggl for two morning study sessions a week), making progress measurable, finding a mentor or buddy for accountability (with quotes from Thinkful's Falina Lothamer), and using small scratch pad projects. The tone is personal and explicitly anti-burnout, ending with a five-step roundup.
